newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Cariplo cuts prime lending rate.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Cariplo cuts prime lending rate.

text.p: Italy's largest savings bank Cariplo said it was cutting its prime lending rate 50 basis points to 8.50 percent and its top lending rate 25 basis points to 15.50 percent from July 7.
Cariplo is the first of Italy's big banks to lower its lending rates below 9.0 percent following a Bank of Italy rate cut of 50 basis points last Friday.
Cariplo said the reduction would also include deposit rates.
Another bank Monte dei Paschi di Siena brought its prime rate down 50 basis points to 9.0 percent on Monday and lowered its top rate by the same amount to 16.75 percent.
Other Italian banks, including San Paolo di Torino, already have prime rates at 9.0 percent or below having cut earlier in the year after the last Bank of Italy rate move in January.
Smaller banks Popolare Novara and Banca Sella have prime rates at 8.75 percent.
The central bank lowered its discount rate to 6.25 percent and its fixed term advances or Lombard rate to 7.75 percent.
